goal: keep the workstation automation fabric healthy using the narrowest owner-specific repair before escalating to physical-console or out-of-band recovery

observedState.resumeCondition: Repair the queue request-authority contract, submit one corrected bounded no-side-effect canary, require a fresh terminal execution receipt, and continue evaluating independent native EVAVO routes meanwhile.

healthyEvidence: resident state is running-cycle or sleeping
corrected queue canary has authoritative successful terminal receipt
selfHeal: repair request authority/schema before changing transport
degradedBehavior: treat a consumed-and-rejected request as transport-live rather than worker-offline
if rejection occurred before execution and receipt says safeAutomaticReplay=true, repair the request contract before changing transport
never replay automatically when sideEffectMayHaveCommitted=true or execution outcome is unknown
do not grow a queue backlog with the same rejected payload shape
continue discovery of other native EVAVO routes capable of the requested operation
allow provider-native read-only operations that do not require the workstation
allow source maintenance and physical-control diagnostics

forbiddenSelfHeal: authority takeover from native EVAVO owner

rules: Health checks should be read-only and non-focus-disruptive whenever possible.
Model transport, request admission, execution and postcondition as separate health phases.
A terminal rejection before execution proves queue transport liveness when the authenticated worker produced the receipt; it does not prove execution readiness.
A component may repair only state it owns.
Self-heal must not silently cross a trust boundary such as hardware profile, identity, firmware, credentials or high-impact recovery authority.
Configured or historically proven authority does not imply current physical liveness.
A source snapshot must never be treated as current machine availability without fresh evidence.
A failed route describes that route only; one failed route cannot prove the MSI or workstation is offline.
Before declaring local execution unavailable, evaluate all native EVAVO routes capable of the requested operation.
Desktop Commander is external fallback only and cannot define workstation health or gate local verification.
Escalation to physical-console control requires evidence that narrower routes are unavailable or insufficient.
A successful process restart is not proof of end-to-end workstation recovery; downstream health must be re-observed.
While one route is degraded, disable unsafe submissions through that route without suppressing independent routes that remain eligible.
